details:
Please consider a client-managed personal video-sharing feature with an SDK component that displays the video on an Avatar surface, without requiring a World video player.

Use case

I am developing PhoneStream, which captures a real Android phone through ADB/scrcpy and displays it on a phone model attached to a VRChat Avatar. A low-resolution version has been tested with a remote friend who did not install additional receiver software. Phone interaction, including taps and swipes, is also implemented.

The remaining limitation is video delivery. My experimental 16x28 four-color mode operates at approximately sub-1 FPS under my test conditions, with 254 of the 256 synced parameter bits allocated. This is not sufficient for readable phone text or fluid scrolling. These are observations from my prototype, not a claim about a fixed platform-wide synchronization rate.

Requested capability

A user explicitly starts a personal media session in the VRChat client. Other users choose to watch it, and VRChat receives and decodes the stream on each consenting viewer's client. A restricted SDK display-binding component maps the decoded video onto a designated Renderer/material slot on the broadcaster's Avatar.

The display should be associated with the Avatar wearer's session, rather than a single shared global texture, so different users can share independent screens.

The feature should not require World authors to install or configure a player. It should still respect viewer preferences and World or instance restrictions.

Suggested initial scope

- PC desktop and PCVR first.

- One outgoing media session per broadcaster.

- A starting evaluation target of 720p at 30 FPS, with higher quality considered later.

- External capture, encoding, and media hosting, subject to VRChat's source policies.

- Explicit viewer opt-in, with client-controlled limits on concurrent decoders, bitrate, resolution, and frame rate.

- Video-only support initially; audio and remote-control integration can be separate future work.

- A placeholder when a session is unavailable, disabled, or unsupported.

PhoneStream can continue handling phone capture, encoding, and its existing phone-control workflow. The requested platform support is session management, authorized media reception and decoding, and Avatar display binding. Protocol and API choices would be up to the VRChat team.

Client controls

Source selection and session authorization should be managed by VRChat's UI. The Avatar component should declare where to display video, without allowing Avatar scripts or animations to silently initiate arbitrary network requests. Viewers should be able to stop reception immediately, and blocking or leaving the session should terminate the associated subscription. Existing moderation and instance controls should apply.

Why existing approaches are insufficient

Avatar state synchronization is not designed for general-purpose video. World players and shared video textures can deliver higher-quality content, but depend on World integration. Local overlays do not make the content visible to friends inside VRChat.

Potential uses include sharing phone content, demonstrating creative work, and discussing applications together without moving to a specially equipped World.

Proposed acceptance test

Two PC users enter a World without a video player. One starts a personal stream; the other opts in. The viewer can see readable text and continuous scrolling on the broadcaster's Avatar phone. Stopping the session or opting out stops reception.

Would this capability fit VRChat's architecture, and what initial scope or constraints would make it practical to evaluate?
title: Personal video streams on Avatar screens without World video players
